question.text: At <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>345</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math>, the half life for the decomposition of a sample of a gaseous compound initially at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>55</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kPa</mi></math> was <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>340</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. When the pressure was <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>27</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kPa</mi></math>, the half life was found to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>170</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. The order of the reaction is - [integer answer]

solution.text:
t1/21t1/22=P1P21-n
